Anika — thanks for the clarity. We've drafted an initial MAP outline and a compact acceptance checklist below to accelerate review. I've copied Marissa for operational signoffs.

Quick summary (top-level success criteria):
- Latency: median P95 < 200ms for 2K concurrent conversational tokens (staging profile).
- Throughput: sustained 300 requests/min on the dedicated pool during stress window.
- Quality: end-to-end response match rate >= 92% against Clarity-provided test set (see acceptance tests).
- Security & compliance: evidence of SOC2 controls held by Redwood (we'll attach extracts), tenant-level audit logging enabled, and optional VPC peering/Private mode configured.

Suggested exit gates (can be staged):
1) Smoke: service reachable, authentication + sample inference pass (3 test prompts).
2) Functional acceptance: 92%+ match on 1000-sample set, no critical data leakage findings.
3) Performance acceptance: P95 and throughput targets met in a controlled test.
4) Security acceptance: SOC2 artifact review + network config validation.

Minimal acceptance tests (we'll provide runnable scripts):
- Sample prompt suite: 500 labeled prompts from Clarity (we need the file) for accuracy checks.
- Latency sweep: synthetic traffic generator with token-length distribution (we'll share the generator config).
- Regression smoke: a set of negative-case prompts to check hallucination frequency and toxic outputs.
- Observability check: verify per-request audit IDs are present and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.

Attachments we'll include in next email: an editable MAP workbook (MAP_v1.xlsx), a short SOC2 extract (SOC2-evidence.pdf), and a draft SOW for procurement review.

Proposed near-term timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (this week): align MAP and acceptance tests, procurement reviews SOW draft
- Week 1: Clarity supplies labeled test set + procurement questions
- Week 2: Joint smoke + functional runs (staging)
- Week 3: Performance/canary test in dedicated pool
- Week 4: Final sign-off & SOW execution

Would you like a kickoff call Wednesday to walk the MAP?

Best,
Evelyn

Adding detail from the CS perspective — I built a concrete acceptance checklist and sign-off owners so there aren't any surprises.

Acceptance checklist (owner in parentheses):
- Smoke test green (Redwood SRE + Clarity Eng) — connectivity, creds, basic inference 3/3 (Evelyn / Clarity Eng)
- Data handling review (Clarity Security + Redwood Security) — confirm no PII persisted, retention config (Marissa / Clarity Sec)
- Quality gate (Product owners) — 92%+ match on the labeled set; manual review for edgecases if 88-92% (Clarity PM + Redwood Product)
- Performance gate (SRE) — P95 <200ms on sample profile; fallback behavior measured under load (Redwood SRE)
- Legal/Procurement gate — SOW agreed, PO issued (Clarity Procurement / Ben on Redwood)

Sign-off flow:
- Each gate requires explicit email sign-off (we'll provide templates). If any gate fails, both parties will run a root-cause call within 48 hours and decide remediation vs rollback.

Operational blockers to flag now:
- We need the labeled test set in CSV format and a preferred auth method for automated runners (API key vs ephemeral token).
- If you plan to test with real patient data, we need a data handling plan and a customer-signed AppSec review window.

I've scheduled a 30-minute kick on Wed 07 Jan 11:00 PT — invite to follow.

-Marissa

Technical acceptance tests and pass criteria (details for Clarity Eng):

1) Functional accuracy test- set: 1,000 labeled prompts (CSV, columns: id, prompt, expected_response_hash). Pass: >=92% exact-match/hash match. If 88-92% run manual adjudication with 200 random samples.

2) Latency / perf profile- runner: we will run the Redwood load harness with your token distribution. Environment: dedicated pool (config: 4xA10G GPUs, batch_size auto, kv_cache enabled). Pass: P95 < 200ms for median token length 64; sustain 300 req/min for 10 min.

3) Stability (long-run)- 24-hour soak with intermittent bursts; pass if no memory OOMs, and rollback time under 2 minutes for node failures.

4) Observability & audit- each request must contain: request_id, tenant_id, model_version. Logs must be exportable as JSON lines. We'll share a small script to validate this.

5) Safety/regression checks- run the provided negative-case suite (50 prompts) — failure threshold: <=2 high-severity hallucinations.

Notes on test data: please strip PII and provide synthetic patient IDs if possible. If you're unable to synthetic-ize the dataset, we can run tests in Private mode with a one-way encrypted drop.

I'll post the test runner repo and a sample config after the kickoff.

-Karthik
